To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the isomerized and inverted Asp residues at positions 4 and 58 of βB2- and αA-crystalls, respectively, in the human lens are biologically relevant and may be responsible for the aging-related changes in the lens.
the aspartate (Asp) at position 4 (Asp-4) in βB2- crystallin from elderly individuals undergoes a high degree of isomerization to biologically uncommon D-β- Asp.

the aspartic acid residues in the α-crystallin and βB2-crystalin proteins of the human eye lens undergo a high degree inversion and isomerisation, resulting in a change in the protein's higher order structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and quantification of post-translational modification of proteins in the human eye lens.
the identification and quantification of the post-translational modification of βB2- and αA-crystalls from human eye lens.
the identification of the specific Asp residues in β-crystallines from human lenses that undergo a high level of inversion and isomeration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isomerized and inverted Asp residues at position 4, 58, and 151 in the crystallins from the aged human lenses have a significant impact on the structure of the proteins and the lens function.
the isomerisation and inversion of Asp-4 in the βB2-crystalin from the aged lens is a post-translational modification of protein that is a direct consequence of ageing.
the isomerized D-β-βB2-crystalls are present in aged human lenses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lens proteins, α- and βB2-crystals, are modified by the same post-translational modification (isomerization and inversion), and the modification is a result of the same mechanism.
the D/L ratio in the Asp residues of crystallin is a good marker of aging in the human eye lens.
the D/L ratio is not a good indicator of the age of a sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Asp residues in the crystallins are prone to undergo inversion.
the isomerized Asp-4 residue may be a new biomarker for aging of the lens.
the lens proteins undergo extensive posttranslational modifications including isomerization and/or inversion of the amino acids.
